author: sonnet
label: c2-nat-sonnet-01
changes: Added an Overview with a glossary (schedule, fire time, run, attempt, lease, reaper, fence) and the shared worker loop, moved up from the Conventions section, so a reader new to the project has the vocabulary first.
Defined the status values and 'in progress' once, right after the diagram.
Reworded the vague tenants-to-job_runs relationship label in the diagram.
Wrote the heartbeat SQL as a code block and made the finishing step say what happens on success and on failure.
Made the fire step an explicit single-transaction numbered list, and split step 4 into the skipped and queued cases.
Replaced 'mutually ordered' with a plain explanation of the FOR SHARE lock, and clarified the claim and cancel race.
Flattened the nested bullets in the pause and disable section and in the constraints list.
Said that the cleanup lock only prevents concurrent cleanup, and used 'retry delay' consistently instead of mixing 'backoff' and 'wait'.
No design changes; all requirements and mechanisms are kept.
Reworded the claim re-check sentence to say plainly that claim and cancellation never both succeed
Replaced 'zombie worker' with 'stale worker' for consistent terminology
Defined 'Run' more plainly and made the fence and lease terms simpler
Made the three-reasons sentence for at-most-one-run easier to parse
Moved the validation sentence to lead with what Postgres cannot check
Smoothed the disable, DST, snapshot and denormalization wording; no design changes
Added a short explanation of FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and FOR SHARE up front, since a reader new to Postgres locking needs them to follow the mechanics.
Defined 'stale worker' and tied 'fence' to the fencing token (attempts_used) in the terms list.
Numbered the four steps of the worker loop instead of one run-on sentence.
Listed the attempt outcome values (including what 'abandoned' means) next to the status list.
Defined 'unstarted' once (queued and attempts_used=0) in the pausing section and reused it, removing duplicated conditions.
Stated explicitly that the worker keeps the new attempts_used value as its attempt number, which the heartbeat and finish queries use as :my_attempt_no.
Clarified why the advisory lock on schedule creation is needed and why the tenant FOR SHARE lock orders pause against fire.
Replaced 'several missed beats' with the concrete figure of about four, and noted that a snapshot means later schedule edits do not affect an existing run.
Tightened wording in a few places (for example the run definition now names the ways a run ends).
